# Pain / Opportunity Analysis — POA-001: Quantifying the Bengali Edition Gap

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Artifact ID | POA-001 |
| Flow Step | 06 — Quantify pain and opportunity (Phase: Problem Discovery) |
| Owner | PA-001 |
| Upstream inputs | IB-001 v1.0, IOH-001 v1.0, PS-001 v3.0, ICP-001 v3.0, RF-001/H-JM-001 v1.0 |
| Reviewers this run | PM-001 (independent), CFO-001/FPA-001 |
| Version | 2.0 (attempt 2 — supersedes attempt 1, returned for low confidence on an evidence-led step) |
| Data sources queried this run | **None.** No analytics platform, no CRM, no billing system, no web research, no interviews (RF-001 reports n=0 participants) |
| Overall confidence | **Medium** — see §0.2 for why this is higher than attempt 1 despite identical (zero) external evidence |
| Evidence quality | **Low** — unchanged and honestly reported; no figure in this artifact is sourced |
| Gate criteria | **MET, on the "strategically important enough to test" limb only — NOT on the "large enough" limb.** See §8. |

---

## 0. What is different in attempt 2, and why confidence moved

### 0.1 Attempt 1's failure

Attempt 1 restated IOH-001's unit economics and IB-001's 230–280M-speaker figure, added a severity adjective, and reported low confidence. It produced no number that could be wrong in a useful way. Restating it more assertively would be a permissions violation for this role — I am never allowed to present a figure derived from no source as reliable.

### 0.2 What I did instead

I cannot import external evidence this run. So I changed the **method**: instead of estimating the opportunity's size (which requires data I don't have), I ran the arithmetic *internal to the artifacts we already possess* and tested them against each other. That is a source I do have, it is reproducible by any reviewer, and it turns out to be productive: **three of the upstream artifacts are quantitatively incompatible with each other, and nobody has noticed because nobody had multiplied the numbers together.**

The three new, internally-verifiable findings:

| # | Finding | Where it comes from | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-1** | **ICP-001's four hard filters are multiplicative and plausibly reduce the global beachhead to ~40 organizations (outer envelope 2–500). IOH-001's kill test K2 requires contacting "40 qualified targets." The GTM test as currently designed may be arithmetically impossible to run.** | §2 | **Critical** |
| **F-2** | **The natural cadence of a Bengali-edition mandate is programme-cycle (≈annual), but IOH-001's kill test K5 requires a repeat order within 90 days. K5 will fire a false kill on a healthy business.** | §3 | High |
| **F-3** | **Severity is bimodal, not continuous. Discretionary "reach" mandates have low, indefinitely-deferrable severity (which is *why* PS-001 observes non-consumption). Only funder-mandated / contractual localization has deadline-driven, price-insensitive severity. The entire viable opportunity concentrates in a slice nobody has sized.** | §4 | High — reframes the ICP |

And one budget finding:

| **F-4** | **IOH-001's $8,000 discovery budget allocates $1,500 to outbound against 40 targets and $1,500 to legal, but $0 to establishing that 40 qualified targets exist. On a value-of-information basis that ordering is inverted.** | §7 | High |

Confidence therefore sits at **Medium overall**: I have **Medium-High** confidence in the arithmetic and the four findings above (they are checkable with a calculator against documents in hand), and **Low** confidence in every input magnitude. Evidence quality remains **Low** and I am not dressing it up. The reason this is decision-useful anyway is §8: the recommended decision is *robust across the entire plausible parameter range*, which I demonstrate rather than assert.

---

## 1. What "pain" and "opportunity" mean here, operationally

Step 06 asks for frequency, severity, affected users and measurable business impact. For a **non-consumption** problem (PS-001 §1), the standard framing needs one correction before the numbers mean anything:

- **Affected users** is *not* the population who would benefit. It is the population who will encounter a **buying moment** — a mandate that reaches a decision point. RF-001's H-JM-001 shows the journey dying at S3–S5 *before* any purchase evaluation. An organization that never reaches S6 is not an affected user in any commercially measurable sense; it is a non-event.
- **Frequency** is *not* how often the pain is felt. It is how often a **forcing event** converts a dormant mandate into a live decision.
